claims_supported.claim: Tracking result is asymptotic only; A.18 is Vdot3 <= -lambda_min(Lambda)V3 + Delta with Delta>0.
Asymptotic tracking only under H(t)==0; time-varying disturbance gives V <= V(0)exp(-gamma t)+varsigma1/gamma.

For constant eta != 0, (x-tilde, eta-tilde) cannot both stay zero; at equilibrium eta-hat = (omega1/omega2)x-tilde and u-hat = eta exactly, so the state error keeps a nonzero offset while the lumped-disturbance estimate is exact.
claims_supported.anchor: Eq.(16), p.9572; derived by substitution, not stated in paper

unverified_or_flagged.item: Eq.(A.2): replacing omega2*eta_i by omega2*D1 requires eta-tilde >= 0 or an absolute-value step; the sign handling is not shown.
Theorem 1 hypothesis (d/dt)|eta-dot_i| <= D2: literal reading is ambiguous; presumably |eta-dot_i| <= D2.

D1,D2 derivation: only the f-dot_i term follows from Assumption 1; the -Proj(Gamma N)phi_i term needs closed-loop boundedness (circular with Theorem 3), the Theta-tilde*phi-dot_i term needs bounded phi-dot_i which fails at u=0 (impulsive u-dot) and near P1->Ps.
Eq.(A.15) yields exact finite-time to s=0, but with d_i != 0 and S_i > 0, s=0 is not invariant; standard STA gives only |s| -> O(D).
Eq.(13)/(14): which part of channel 2 is chi_2 vs Theta*phi_2 is not specified; phi_2 appears to contain u through phi5, so the 'disturbance' eta_2 depends on the control input.
Gamma defined as 3x3 in Eq.(11) but experiment C1 lists 6 diagonal entries.
Eq.(16) printed equality keeps only the delta_2 term of varsigma and drops the l3|u|max/(4w0^2) term.
u_n-dot = -beta2 sign(s)/2 in Eq.(20) vs -beta2 sign(s) in Eq.(22); changes the factor 2 in Q.
Theorem 3 Barbalat step requires (51) globally, but adaptive law (21) can drop beta1 below threshold (25) when |s|<v, making Q indefinite (case S2).
Assumption 1 bounds |d-dot| but d in Eq.(6) contains -f-dot/m, so boundedness of |f-double-dot| is implicitly required.
No assumption stated on x1d being C^3 with bounded derivatives, although x3eq-dot is used in (20).

prohibited_inferences_enforced: PE is not treated as a finite-time identification guarantee.
Observer convergence is not treated as a necessary condition for exact tracking.
V-dot <= -a V^p + b with b>0 is not read as exact convergence to zero.
Finite-time reaching of the sliding surface is not equated with finite-time position regulation.
